note: Common incorrect statements per key point. Patterns are lower-case regular expressions matched per sentence; a negation just before the match (not, never, avoid, instead of, misconception, ...) suppresses it. Curated, not exhaustive.

python-e1.note: Lists are mutable and tuples are immutable, not the other way round.
Lists are not hashable and cannot be dictionary keys; tuples of hashable items can.
Lists use square brackets; tuples use parentheses.

python-m1.note: Generators produce items lazily and use less memory than building a full list.

python-h1.note: A decorator wraps a function; it does not edit the original source code.

java-e1.note: A Java class can implement many interfaces but extend only one class.
Abstract classes can have fields and constructors.

java-m1.note: HashMap does not guarantee any order (use TreeMap or LinkedHashMap for ordering).

java-h1.note: Java can still leak memory when references are kept unintentionally.
The garbage collector only frees objects that are no longer reachable.

cpp-e1.note: A pointer can be null and reassigned; a reference cannot.

cpp-m1.note: With RAII the destructor runs automatically when the object goes out of scope.

cpp-h1.note: std::move only casts to an rvalue reference; the move constructor or assignment does the transfer.

js-e1.note: let and const are block-scoped; var is function-scoped.
A const binding cannot be reassigned (although an object it points to can be mutated).

js-m1.note: await pauses only the async function; the thread and event loop keep running.

js-h1.note: JavaScript runs your code on a single thread with a call stack.
Microtasks (promise callbacks) run before macrotasks such as timers.

ts-e1.note: TypeScript checks types at compile time; types are erased at runtime.
Browsers run the JavaScript that TypeScript compiles to.

ts-m1.note: Interfaces can be extended and merged; type aliases cannot be merged.

ts-h1.note: Generics keep type safety, unlike any.

kotlin-e1.note: Kotlin types are non-nullable by default.
!! throws if the value is null; prefer ?. and ?:.

kotlin-m1.note: Data classes generate equals, hashCode, toString and copy automatically.

kotlin-h1.note: suspend functions pause without blocking a thread; coroutines are lighter than threads.

swift-e1.note: Force unwrapping crashes if the value is nil.
An optional can hold nil; that is its purpose.

swift-m1.note: Structs are value types; classes are reference types.
Only classes support inheritance in Swift.

swift-h1.note: Protocol extensions can provide default implementations.

html-e1.note: Semantic elements help screen readers and other assistive technology.

html-m1.note: Placeholders are not a substitute for labels.

patterns: \bblock elements? (?:flow|stay) (?:inline|in the text|on the same line)
html-h1.note: Block elements start on a new line; inline elements flow within text.

css-e1.note: Padding is inside the border; margin is outside it.
border-box includes padding and border in the declared width.
Vertical margins can collapse; padding does not.

css-m1.note: Flexbox is one-dimensional; Grid is two-dimensional.

css-h1.note: IDs beat classes, which beat element selectors.
When specificity ties, the later rule wins.

bootstrap-m1.note: Customise through variables or your own CSS rather than editing Bootstrap's files.

bootstrap-h1.note: Frameworks add CSS weight unless you import only what you use.

tailwind-e1.note: Tailwind provides utility classes, not pre-built components.

tailwind-m1.note: Tailwind is mobile-first: unprefixed classes apply at all sizes.

react-e1.note: Props are read-only for the component that receives them.

react-m1.note: useEffect runs after the component renders.
An empty array runs the effect once after mount; no array runs it after every render.

rn-e1.note: React Native renders native components, not HTML in a web view.

rn-h1.note: FlatList virtualises long lists; ScrollView renders everything at once.

angular-h1.note: OnPush reduces checks; it does not run change detection more often.

vue-m1.note: Computed properties are cached; watchers run side effects.

node-e1.note: Node.js uses non-blocking, event-driven I/O rather than a thread per request.
Node.js is a JavaScript runtime, not a language.

node-h1.note: CPU-heavy work blocks the event loop even inside an async function.

django-e1.note: Views handle requests; templates render HTML.

django-m1.note: makemigrations creates migration files; migrate applies them.

django-h1.note: select_related uses a SQL join for foreign keys; prefetch_related runs a separate query.

fastapi-h1.note: Blocking calls inside async def stall the event loop; async is not automatically faster.
Plain def endpoints run in a thread pool, so they do not block the event loop.

spring-e1.note: Spring Boot includes an embedded server.

patterns: \b(?:does not|doesn't|never) roll back on runtime exceptions
spring-h1.note: @Transactional rolls back on runtime (unchecked) exceptions by default, not checked ones.

rest-m1.note: 4xx codes are client errors and 5xx codes are server errors.
201 means Created and 204 means No Content.

rest-h1.note: GET, PUT and DELETE are idempotent; POST is not.

graphql-e1.note: GraphQL usually exposes a single endpoint.

graphql-m1.note: Queries read data; mutations change it.

sql-e1.note: INNER JOIN returns only the rows that match in both tables.
LEFT JOIN returns every row from the left table, matched or not.
NULLs for missing matches come from outer joins such as LEFT JOIN.

sql-m1.note: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after.
Aggregate conditions belong in HAVING, not WHERE.

sql-h1.note: Indexes speed up reads but slow down writes and use storage.

sqlite-e1.note: SQLite is serverless: the database is a single file.

patterns: \bsqlite (?:is|is good|is great|works well) (?:for|at|with) (?:many|lots of|high) concurrent writ
sqlite-e1.note: SQLite allows one writer at a time, so it is not ideal for many concurrent writers.

sqlite-m1.note: SQLite uses type affinity; strict typing needs STRICT tables.

sqlite-h1.note: SQLite allows only one writer at a time.

firebase-e1.note: Firestore is a NoSQL document database.

firebase-m1.note: Firestore stores documents in collections and has no SQL joins.

firebase-h1.note: Clients reach the database directly, so security rules are essential.

aws-e1.note: EC2 provides virtual servers; S3 stores objects.

aws-m1.note: Least privilege means granting only the permissions that are needed.
Avoid long-lived keys in code; use roles.

aws-h1.note: High availability needs multiple Availability Zones.

azure-e1.note: Deleting a resource group deletes everything in it.

azure-m1.note: App Service is managed PaaS; VMs (IaaS) give full OS control.

azure-h1.note: Store secrets in Key Vault and use managed identities, not code.

gcp-e1.note: Compute Engine provides VMs; Cloud Storage stores objects.

gcp-m1.note: Cloud Run is serverless: you do not manage servers.

docker-e1.note: An image is the read-only template; a container is a running instance of it.
A container is an instance of an image, not the other way round.
Many containers can run from one image.

docker-m1.note: Copy dependency files first so the dependency layer stays cached.

docker-h1.note: Data in a container's writable layer is lost when the container is removed; use volumes.

k8s-e1.note: A Pod can run one or more containers.
A Service provides a stable network address; Pods run the containers.

k8s-m1.note: Kubernetes Secrets are base64-encoded; encryption at rest must be enabled.
Sensitive values belong in Secrets, not ConfigMaps.

k8s-h1.note: Liveness probes restart containers; readiness probes control traffic.

terraform-m1.note: State can contain secrets: store it remotely and protect it, not in Git.

jenkins-e1.note: Jenkins automates builds, tests and deployments; it is not version control.

jenkins-m1.note: A Jenkinsfile lives in the repository.

jenkins-h1.note: Inject credentials from the store instead of hard-coding them.

cicd-e1.note: CI is about merging and testing often; CD keeps code deployable.

cicd-h1.note: Sending a small share of traffic to a new version is a canary release, not blue-green.
Switching all traffic between two environments is blue-green, not canary.

linux-e1.note: chmod changes permissions; chown changes ownership.

linux-h1.note: journalctl reads logs; systemctl manages services.

net-e1.note: UDP is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery or order.

net-h1.note: The prefix length is the number of network bits; a /24 has 256 addresses.

monitoring-e1.note: Metrics are numeric measurements; logs record events; traces follow requests.

monitoring-m1.note: Alerting on everything causes fatigue; alert on user-facing symptoms.

monitoring-h1.note: SLI is the measurement, SLO the target, SLA the agreement with consequences.

git-e1.note: Merge adds a merge commit; rebase rewrites history into a linear sequence.
Avoid rebasing branches others are using.

git-h1.note: Protect main and merge through reviewed pull requests.

ml-e1.note: Supervised learning uses labelled data (classification, regression).
Unsupervised learning works on unlabelled data (clustering).

ml-m1.note: Overfitting is fitting the training data too closely; a too-simple model underfits.
Underfitting is a model too simple to capture the patterns.

ml-h1.note: Accuracy is misleading on imbalanced data.

dl-m1.note: Gradients flow backwards with the chain rule and update the weights.

dl-h1.note: Dropout is active only during training.
Early stopping monitors a validation set.

nlp-e1.note: Tokens can be words, subwords or characters.

nlp-m1.note: Embeddings are dense vectors, unlike sparse one-hot encodings.

nlp-h1.note: Attention looks at all tokens at once, which allows parallel computation.

cv-m1.note: Augment the training data, not the test data used for evaluation.

cv-h1.note: Detection draws bounding boxes; segmentation labels pixels.
Segmentation labels each pixel rather than drawing boxes.

tf-e1.note: Train on training data and keep the test data for evaluation.

pytorch-m1.note: Call zero_grad, then backward, then optimizer.step.

pytorch-h1.note: eval() changes layer behaviour; torch.no_grad() disables gradient tracking.

sklearn-e1.note: Fit on training data; evaluate on held-out test data.

sklearn-m1.note: Fitting preprocessing on all data before splitting leaks information; pipelines prevent this.

sklearn-h1.note: Tune with cross-validation and keep the test set for the final check.

pandas-m1.note: dropna removes missing values; fillna fills them.

pandas-h1.note: merge joins DataFrames; groupby groups rows within one DataFrame.

numpy-e1.note: NumPy's vectorised operations avoid Python-level loops.

numpy-m1.note: Broadcasting stretches dimensions without copying data.
Broadcasting compares dimensions from the right.

numpy-h1.note: Basic slicing returns a view that shares memory.
Changing a view changes the original array.

stats-e1.note: The median is robust to outliers; the mean is not.
The mode is the most frequent value.

stats-m1.note: A p-value is the probability of data this extreme if the null is true, not the probability the null is true.
A small p-value is evidence, not proof.

stats-h1.note: Correlation does not by itself establish causation.

da-m1.note: Investigate outliers before deciding to remove, cap or keep them.

excel-e1.note: Relative references change when copied; $ makes a reference absolute.
Absolute references stay fixed when a formula is copied.

excel-m1.note: VLOOKUP only looks to the right; use XLOOKUP or INDEX/MATCH to look left.

excel-h1.note: Pivot tables must be refreshed after the source data changes.

powerbi-h1.note: Measures are evaluated at query time in the filter context.
Calculated columns are computed per row and stored.

tableau-e1.note: Dimensions are categorical fields used to group.
Measures are numeric values that are aggregated.

ds-e1.note: Arrays give O(1) access by index; linked lists need O(n).
Arrays use contiguous memory; linked lists use separate nodes.

ds-m1.note: Hash tables give average O(1) operations and do not keep keys sorted.

ds-h1.note: Peek is O(1); a heap is only partially ordered.

algo-e1.note: Big-O describes growth rate, not exact time.

algo-h1.note: Dynamic programming reuses solutions to overlapping subproblems; it is neither greedy nor brute force.

selenium-m1.note: Implicit waits set a global timeout; explicit waits wait for a condition.
Explicit waits target one condition, not a global timeout.
Fixed sleeps make tests slow and flaky.

figma-e1.note: Instances update when the main component changes.

wireframe-h1.note: Mockups are static; prototypes add interaction.

ur-e1.note: Qualitative research explores why; quantitative measures how many.
Quantitative research measures how many or how much.

agile-m1.note: The review and retrospective happen at the end of the sprint.

mr-h1.note: TAM is the total market; SOM is the share you can realistically obtain.

fm-e1.note: The income statement shows revenue, costs and profit.
The balance sheet shows assets, liabilities and equity.
Profit is not the same as cash flow.

fm-h1.note: Future cash is worth less today, which is why it is discounted.

seo-e1.note: Keyword stuffing hurts rankings; write relevant content.
